text:
morgan: heads up, we're seeing a correlated spike in GPU attach latency and a huge small-write iops tail in us-central1 around 09:10 UTC :warning:
infra-bot: alert: attach_latency.p95 > 750ms for 12m in us-central1 (affected pools: gpu-preemptible-*)
sasha: looks like the tempstore writers are churning lots of tiny files right before the attach window, small_write_iops going to 90k
alex: can confirm, dug into node gnode-cc34: kernel logs show a bunch of overlayfs fsync stalls and repeated writeback bursts
alex: snippet: ```kernel: overlayfs: writeback: 3.4ms avg, max 220ms
kern: vfs_fsync: delayed -> queued flush```
jean: that fits a pattern we saw last month but not identical — janitor process is aggressive and when attach happens the scheduler tries to reclaim which causes fanout deletes and more fsyncs
morgan: so a feedback loop: attach waits -> processes flush -> janitor deletes tempfiles -> IO spikes -> attach waits longer -> autoscaler requeues -> more tempfiles? :exploding_head:
ryan: can we throttle janitor deletes temporarily for the affected pools? there's a config flag `delete_concurrency` for tempstore-janitor
sasha: yes we can patch to set delete_concurrency=4 and delete_rate=250/s, down from 16/1000. that'll reduce delete fanout.
alex: quick mitigation we can roll: ```kubectl -n infra set env deployment/tempstore-janitor DELETE_CONCURRENCY=4 DELETE_RATE=250``` then restart.
morgan: also worth toggling the overlayfs commit interval on the hot nodes: `echo 1500 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_writeback_centisecs` — lowers sync frequency -> fewer big bursts
jean: be careful: lowering too far increases memory pressure. i'd rather reduce janitor first, monitor for 10m.
oncall-bot: scheduled: tempstore-janitor patch rollout at 09:25 UTC (morgan)
ryan: I'll schedule the rollout and watch attach latency and small_write_iops. if it doesn't improve, fallback is enabling a small-write coalescer on the tempstore writer (needs a code change)
sasha: can we also blacklist the most aggressive pod owners temporarily? top writers list shows test-runner jobs spamming small files
alex: command: `/usr/local/bin/tempstore-stats --top 10` returns the offending pods; i've added a quick acl to limit their parallelism to 1
morgan: ok proceeding with the janitor env change now. will post updates here. thanks all :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy started: tempstore-janitor v2.3.1 -> rolling update (3 replicas)
ryan: update 09:32 UTC: after throttling, small_write_iops dropped from ~90k -> ~22k, attach p95 improved to 310ms. still above baseline but trending down
jean: great signal. follow-up: create a mini-postmortem and add a safemode for janitor when attach latency > 500ms (auto-throttle)
morgan: agreed. i'll open a ticket and assign owners. root cause hypothesis: aggressive janitor concurrency + overlayfs commit heuristics + a bursty test job pattern causing a feedback loop
morgan: ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8372 (will fill in details)
oncall-bot: incident auto-closed after stabilization at 09:45 UTC
